open_points.subject: A03 rule 5 process-count bound
open_points.text: the process count by the runner inside the environment's user namespace before the code loads, at `process_count` plus one
open_points.question: Which tasks count against `process_count`, and which single task is the added one—does the bound include the runner, bubblewrap's PID-namespace supervisor, child processes, and Python threads, or does it mean only tasks created by agent code?
options: `process_count` counts all tasks including the runner, with one explicitly exempt infrastructure task
`process_count` counts tasks created by agent code, and the added one is the runner
Use the kernel's RLIMIT_NPROC accounting literally, including any runner, supervisor, process, or thread it counts
open_points.default_guess: Configure the sandbox so the runner is the only counted infrastructure task and treat `process_count` as the maximum additional tasks agent code may create.

open_points.subject: A03 rules 5 and 8 process-limit isolation
open_points.text: since a process limit set by the parent counts every process of the kernel's user on the host and the namespace could not be created ... The start probe (rule 8) sets its limits at the current ceilings the same way
open_points.question: Must startup verify that the host kernel accounts the runner's process limit within its user namespace rather than against the host-wide kernel user, and what happens if setting the limit succeeds but that isolation property does not hold?
options: Probe namespace-local process accounting and refuse startup if it is absent
Assume every host capable of running bubblewrap supplies namespace-local accounting
Allow host-wide accounting and let affected executions become `resource_exhausted` or `crashed`
open_points.default_guess: Probe the accounting behavior at startup and refuse to start when it is not namespace-local.

open_points.subject: A03 rule 5 capability boundary
open_points.text: the code runs without capabilities (bubblewrap's default for an unprivileged caller, never overridden), so it can neither raise nor bypass a limit
open_points.question: How is the absence of capabilities guaranteed across host bubblewrap versions, given that rule 8 checks only that bubblewrap is present and a probe succeeds while A20 says dependency versions are fixed?
options: Require and check an exact bubblewrap version whose default is part of the release
Use explicit capability-dropping configuration and probe the resulting capability set
Rely on whatever default the installed bubblewrap version provides
open_points.default_guess: Explicitly drop all capabilities and make the startup probe verify the resulting capability set.
